Compute Match — Product Overview
What is Compute Match?
Compute Match, also called the Compute MatchMake System (internal project key NCPMS, code name Clustrufﬂe), is
an NVIDIA web platform that connects customers who need GPU compute capacity with NVIDIA Cloud Providers (NCPs)
who own and operate GPU infrastructure.
In one sentence: customers ﬁnd GPU clusters, send reservation requests, and NCPs accept, negotiate, and contract those
requests, while NVIDIA Platform Admins oversee the marketplace.

The core idea in ﬁve steps
1. NCPs publish capacity. An NCP uploads a CSV describing how many GPUs of which platform (for example H100,
B200, GB200) are available, in which country and city, and from which date.
2. Customers search. A customer opens Find a Cluster to Reserve, ﬁlters by platform, region, country, GPU count,
tenure, and earliest start date, and sees matching clusters on a world map and as cards.
3. Customers request. The customer submits a reservation request for one cluster, or for up to 3 clusters from
different NCPs at once (multi-NCP request). If nothing ﬁts, they submit a custom request that NVIDIA admins broker
manually.
4. NCPs respond. Each selected NCP receives an email with a secure magic link. The NCP accepts (moving the
request to In Process), rejects, or counteroffers, and ﬁnally clicks Conﬁrm Contract.
5. Contract. The ﬁrst NCP to contract wins; the other NCPs’ offerings on the same request are cancelled as
superseded. Capacity is allocated, and the deal is synced to Salesforce as an Offtake record.

Important timers (defaults)
An NCP has 7 days to accept a request routed to them (acceptance window).
After accepting, the NCP and customer have 45 days to reach a contract (contract negotiation window).
Reminder emails are sent 3 days before each deadline.
A magic link is valid for 1 hour, and can be regenerated for up to 7 days after routing.
Custom requests never expire automatically.
Platform Admins can extend either window by 1 to 200 days.
Technology at a glance
Frontend: Next.js 15, React 19, Ant Design 6, Tailwind CSS 4, NextAuth 5 with Keycloak.
Backend: Python 3.13, FastAPI, Domain-Driven Design with hexagonal architecture, SQLAlchemy, PostgreSQL,
Alembic migrations.
Workﬂows: Temporal (Temporal Cloud in shared environments) with a Python workﬂow worker.
Identity: Keycloak with NVIDIA Starﬂeet SSO, custom Keycloak extensions.
Analytics: Apache Superset dashboards.
Platform: Google Cloud — GKE Autopilot, Cloud SQL PostgreSQL, Memorystore Redis, Secret Manager; deployed
with Terraform and Helm through GitLab CI.
Integrations: Salesforce (Offtake sync and partner-domain sync), email notiﬁcations.
Where to get help
In the app: Page Help (the ?  icon) for context help and User Manual (book icon) for the full role-ﬁltered manual.
Support email for access problems: computematchmake@nvidia.com.
Developer docs: the docs/  folder in the repository, also published as the Compute Match documentation site.

Compute Match — Signing Up, Signing In and First-Time
Setup
How sign-in works
Compute Match uses Starﬂeet, NVIDIA’s single sign-on service, through Keycloak. Sign up and Login use the same ﬂow.
1. Open the home page and click Get Started, Sign up or Login.
2. On the /login  page enter your Work email and click Login.
3. Personal email domains (Gmail, Yahoo, Hotmail and similar) are blocked with an explanation. Use your work or
enterprise email.
4. You are redirected to Starﬂeet and your organization’s identity provider (for example NVIDIA corporate login or your
company SSO).
5. After authentication you return to Compute Match. You may brieﬂy pass through several authentication pages; this is
normal.
Technically, the frontend uses NextAuth 5 with the Keycloak client customer-web  in the customer  realm, and passes
kc_idp_hint=starfleet  to send users to the Starﬂeet identity broker.

activated.
Your access is being reviewed ( /access-pending ). Your company is an NVIDIA partner but its NCP organization is

NCP sign-in paths
Welcome email
New NCP users created by NCP onboarding receive a provider_welcome  email with a direct login link.
Magic link (respond to a reservation)
When a reservation request is routed to an NCP, users in that NCP organization who have the provider_business_user  role
and belong to the offering-validator  group get an email with a magic link.
1. The link is a Keycloak action token created by the custom accept-reservation-token  extension.
2. Keycloak validates the token and a one-time nonce with the backend ( POST /api/v1/offering/validate-nonce ), blocks
the link if a different user is already logged in, creates a session and redirects.
3. The browser lands on /automatic-login?from=magic-link&callbackUrl=... , which skips the email page and reuses the
SSO session, then opens Manage reservation so the NCP can Accept.
4. A magic link is valid for 1 hour. NCPs or admins can resend one ( POST /api/v1/provider/offering/{offeringId}/resend-
magic-link ) within 7 days of routing.
NPN portal
NVIDIA Partner Network (NPN) members can reach Compute Match directly from the NPN portal (feature ﬂag
NPN_PORTAL_INTEGRATION_ENABLED ). They still pass through the work-email page and Starﬂeet. If their partner organization is
not onboarded yet, an access request with source NPN_PORTAL  is created and they wait on the access-pending page.
How partner detection works
Compute Match keeps a partner domain mirror of email domains belonging to NVIDIA partners, synced from
Salesforce twice a day.
Domain lookup statuses are PARTNER , NOT_PARTNER  and PENDING .
Personal mail providers can never be partner domains.
When a user from a partner domain signs up and their NCP is not onboarded, POST /api/v1/user  creates an access
request (statuses PENDING , APPROVED , REJECTED ; sources NPN_PORTAL , SIGNUP ).
A Platform Admin approves or rejects it under Onboard NCPs →  Review Onboarding Requests. Approval
provisions the organization and user in Keycloak; rejection emails the reason. A rejected applicant can apply again,
which creates a new request.
Signing out
Use Logout in the account menu. If your session cannot be refreshed, the app shows a recovery screen and performs a full
Keycloak logout.

1. Click Download Template.

CSV rules
UTF-8 CSV, at most 10 MB and 10,000 data rows, each cell at most 500 characters.
Required columns: GPU Platform Type , Number of GPUs Available , Live Token Date , Country , City .
Optional columns: Region , end_datetime .
Metadata columns that are accepted but ignored: NCP Name , RA/RD , Exemplar Cluster , aaS Capability , State .
The hosting provider name comes from your NCP organization, not from the CSV.
Vendor preﬁxes like “NVIDIA” in the platform cell are tolerated; country names such as “USA” or “Holland” are
normalized.
Cells beginning with = , + , -  or @  are neutralized to prevent spreadsheet formula injection.
Invalid rows are skipped with errors listed; the job fails only if no row succeeds.
Current versus future capacity
Rows whose Live Token Date is within 90 days of upload are current (AVAILABLE) capacity and go live immediately
after validation.
Rows starting more than 90 days out are future (FUTURE) capacity. The job waits in Pending Review until a
Platform Admin accepts or rejects it. You are emailed the result and any rejection reason appears in the Details
column.

Catalog / multi-NCP ﬂow, step by step
1. Customer submits ( POST /api/v1/reservation-request ). The backend creates the request and the customer’s ﬁrst
proposal, then routes it: one offering per selected cluster (backend limit 10, UI limit 3 by default).
2. Each offering starts as AwaitingProviderAcceptance with acceptance_expiry_date = now + 7 days . The request
becomes AwaitingProviderAcceptance.
3. Temporal starts a parent ReservationRequestWorkflow  and one child OfferingLifecycleWorkflow  per offering. The
customer gets a “request received” email; each NCP gets a magic-link email.
4. NCP accepts →  offering InProcess, contract_expiry_date = now + 45 days , NCP and customer receive an
introduction email. The ﬁrst acceptance moves the request to InProcess.
5. NCP counteroffers →  a new proposal is recorded (price-only changes update in place; material changes create a
new proposal in history).
6. NCP conﬁrms contract →  offering Contracted, an Allocation is created (status scheduled ), the request becomes
Contracted, and sibling offerings are Cancelled with “superseded” emails.
7. NCP rejects (remarks required) →  offering Rejected. If all offerings are rejected, the request is Rejected.
8. Timers: if an NCP does not accept in 7 days →  offering Expired. If no contract in 45 days →  offering Expired. When
every offering has expired, the customer gets one consolidated expiry email and the request becomes Expired.
Reminders go out 3 days before each deadline.
9. Customer cancels →  request Cancelled; NCPs are notiﬁed.
10. Extensions: a Platform Admin (scope accept_contract_extension ) can extend acceptance or contract deadlines by 1–
200 days; this can revive an Expired offering.

Capacity rules that affect requests
Capacity windows of the same type (AVAILABLE or FUTURE) cannot partially overlap; at most one open-ended
window per type.
Availability checks use the upper bound of the tenure band (for example 2-3  years is checked as 3 years) to be
conservative.
Allocations only subtract from the matching capacity type.
An optional cap ( MAX_PENDING_REQUESTS_PER_REGIONAL_CAPACITY , default 0 = unlimited) hides clusters with too many
pending requests and rejects new requests against them.
GPU count per request must be between 1 and 100,000.
Contracted price must be zero or positive and is only visible to NCPs and NVIDIA admins.

CSV capacity import — end-to-end ﬂow
1. Upload. An NCP with manage_inventory  uploads a CSV on Upload Capacities ( POST /api/v1/provider/gpu-
offerings/import , returns 202 Accepted). The backend checks size (10 MB) and row count (10,000).
2. Job created. An ImportJob  is stored with status QUEUED , and Temporal workﬂow CsvImportWorkflow  starts with id csv-
import-{job_id} .
3. Validate. The worker validates columns and rows ( VALIDATING ). If nothing is valid →  VALIDATION_FAILED .
4. Import. Valid rows are imported atomically ( IMPORTING ). Failures here →  IMPORT_FAILED .
5. Classify. Rows starting within 90 days of upload become AVAILABLE  and are published immediately. Rows starting
later become FUTURE .
6. Review (future only). If there are new future rows, the job moves to PENDING_REVIEW , admins are emailed, and the
workﬂow waits for an approve_import  or reject_import  signal.
7. Decision. A Platform Admin with review_capacity  accepts ( APPROVED  then COMPLETED , offerings activated) or rejects
( REJECTED  / FUTURE_CAPACITY_REJECTED , with reason).
8. Notify. The NCP is emailed the result.

Magic links in detail
Recipients: users of the NCP organization with role provider_business_user  and in group offering-validator . Basic
users never receive them.
The backend asks the Keycloak extension endpoint POST /realms/{realm}/clustruffle/create-action-token  to mint an
action token containing the offering id and a nonce.
When clicked, Keycloak validates the nonce with the backend, logs the user in and redirects with from=magic-link .
Valid 1 hour; resend possible for 7 days after routing.
Magic-link emails use the critical retry policy (10 attempts over about 25 minutes) because they are the only way an
NCP learns about a request.
Reliability
Ordinary notiﬁcations retry 5 times over about 2.5 minutes.
Permanent failures are absorbed (and counted in metric clustruffle_workflow_activity_abandoned ) so a workﬂow
replay never re-sends email to users.

ReservationRequestWorkﬂow
1. Send “request received” email to the customer.
2. Wait for signal routed_to_providers  or reservation_request_closed . Open/custom requests wait indeﬁnitely.
3. On routing, start one child OfferingLifecycleWorkflow  per offering.
4. Wait until any child is Contracted, all children ﬁnish, or the parent is closed.
5. If one contracts: cancel siblings (superseded) and approve the request.
6. If all expire: send one consolidated customer expiry email and expire the request.
7. Closure reasons send emails: Cancelled (customer + NCPs), Rejected, Matched, Unserviceable.
Signals: routed_to_providers , reservation_request_closed . Child workﬂow retry up to 100 attempts; expire activity 20
attempts over about 75 minutes.
OfferingLifecycleWorkﬂow
1. Send the magic-link email (critical retry policy).
2. Acceptance phase (7 days by default): reminder 3 days before; on timeout expire the offering and email the NCP.
3. On provider_accepted : send the introduction email; start the contract phase (45 days).
4. Reminder 3 days before contract expiry; on timeout expire and email.
5. On offering_contracted : send contracted email. On reject or cancel: handle and email (superseded if a sibling won).
Signals: provider_accepted , acceptance_expiry_extended , contract_expiry_extended , offering_contracted , offering_rejected ,
offering_cancelled .
CsvImportWorkﬂow
VALIDATING →  IMPORTING →  (if future rows) PENDING_REVIEW: email admins and wait for approve_import  /
reject_import  →  activate or reject offerings →  email the NCP. Activities: validate_csv , execute_atomic_import ,
activate_offerings , reject_offerings , update_import_job_status , notify_admin_for_review , notify_provider_result .
Workﬂow max attempts 1; import activities 3 attempts.
ProviderOnboardingWorkﬂow
validate_provider_csv  →  execute_provider_onboarding  (30-minute timeout) →  notify_onboarding_complete  (sent even on
failure). 3 attempts; validation errors are not retried.
Salesforce workﬂows
SfdcCreateBatchWorkflow  drains the salesforce_create_sync  outbox. Create mode retries 13 times every 5 minutes;
status mode runs once per tick. Gated by SFDC_SYNC_ENABLED ; when false, schedules are deleted and the workﬂow is
not registered.
SfdcPartnerDomainSyncWorkflow  is gated by SFDC_PARTNER_DOMAIN_SYNC_ENABLED . It refuses empty or suspiciously shrunk
snapshots so partners are not mass-demoted.

Compute Match — Security, Observability, Salesforce
Integration and Testing
Security model
Delivery identity: GitLab OIDC with Google Workload Identity Federation; separate Google service accounts for plan,
apply, deploy, verify and Keycloak.
Runtime identity: Kubernetes service accounts mapped to Google service accounts; secrets from Secret Manager
with least privilege; Cloud SQL Auth Proxy; separate database roles (for example the audit-retention role can only
SELECT and DELETE).
Network: NetworkPolicies, private Cloud SQL and Redis, Cloud Armor and Gateway at the edge.
Application: Keycloak JWTs with audiences per client ( customer-web , workflow-worker , audit-listener …). Internal
Salesforce and audit endpoints only accept a pinned caller client_id . CSV cells are sanitized against formula
injection. Personal email domains are blocked.
Repository: protected main , CODEOWNERS, secret scanning (gitleaks, trufﬂehog, talisman), no secrets in
manifests or docs.
Audit: Keycloak login/logout events and domain actions are written to an audit log, kept about 13 months then purged
by AuditRetentionWorkflow .
Observability
Logs: every owned service writes JSON Lines to stdout using Log Record v2 ( docs/architecture/logging/log-record-
v2.md ): log_schema_version: 2 , severity, event_name , resource, source, optional trace context, attributes and exception.
Unsafe ﬁelds are redacted; no PII or secrets in attributes.
Event catalog ( docs/architecture/logging/event-catalog.md ): for example workflow.started , workflow.completed ,
workflow.failed , reservation.request.* , csv_import.* , provider_onboarding.* , integration.salesforce.failed ,
notification.delivery.failed , authorization.denied .
Traces and metrics: OpenTelemetry in frontend, backend, worker (Temporal TracingInterceptor) and Keycloak. In
GCP the Helm otel-collector  exports to Google Cloud; logs go to Cloud Logging. Locally, optional SigNoz ( make obs-
start , UI on port 3301).
Runbooks: docs/operations/*-observability.md  for backend, frontend, worker, Keycloak, Superset and gateway.
Salesforce integration (ADR-001)
Direction: one-way, Compute Match →  Salesforce Offtake object ( Offtake_Request__c ).
Pattern: transactional outbox table salesforce_create_sync , drained by Temporal SfdcCreateBatchWorkflow  which calls
backend internal APIs (domain stays in the backend). No Kafka or Pub/Sub.
Granularity: one Offtake per NCP offering (external id Reservation_Request_Offering_Id__c ); open custom requests
get one create-only Offtake keyed by the request id.
Jobs: nightly create (05:00 UTC, full projection) and status every 2 minutes (status and, when Contracted,
negotiated terms). Upserts use the sObject Collections external-id API, up to 200 records per call.
Reliability: outbox states PENDING, SYNCED, FAILED; retries for Salesforce outages; mandatory failure summary
email; audit events SFDC_OFFTAKE_SYNCED  / SFDC_OFFTAKE_SYNC_FAILED  written atomically with the outbox.
Toggles: SFDC_SYNC_ENABLED ; partner-domain read sync separately with SFDC_PARTNER_DOMAIN_SYNC_ENABLED .

Frequently asked questions
How do I sign up? Click Sign up or Login, enter your work email, and sign in through Starﬂeet. Personal emails are not
allowed.
Why do I see “Access denied”? Your identity was veriﬁed but your account is not authorized under current policies.
Contact computematchmake@nvidia.com or sign in with another work account.
Why do I see “Your access is being reviewed”? Your company is an NVIDIA partner but its NCP organization is not on
the platform yet. A Platform Admin must approve your access request.
How many NCPs can I send one request to? Up to 3 in the UI by default (backend allows up to 10), if you have the multi-
NCP permission.
Will I get several contracts if I send to several NCPs? No. The options are alternatives; the ﬁrst NCP to conﬁrm the
contract wins and the others are cancelled.
How long does an NCP have to respond? 7 days to accept, then 45 days to contract. Reminders arrive 3 days before
each deadline. Admins can extend both.
My magic link says it expired. Links last 1 hour. Ask for a resend (possible for 7 days after routing) or log in normally and
open Manage reservation.
Can I accept an NCP counteroffer as a customer? The customer detail page is view and cancel only; the NCP conﬁrms
the contract after you agree with them directly.
When can I cancel? While the request is Awaiting NCP Acceptance, awaiting approval, In Process or Expired; custom
requests while Open or In Review.
What if no cluster matches my needs? Submit a custom request. Admins will review and mark it Matched or
Unserviceable.
My CSV upload shows Pending Review. It contains future capacity (starting more than 90 days out); a Platform Admin
must accept it.
My CSV upload shows Validation Failed. Open “See all details” for row errors. Check the ﬁve required columns, UTF-8
encoding, 10 MB and 10,000-row limits.
Why can’t I see Upload Capacities or Manage reservation? You lack the scope ( manage_inventory  or
approver_manage_reservation_request ). Basic NCP users are read-only. Ask your Platform Admin.
I have customer and NCP access. How do I switch? Use Switch proﬁle to at the top of the account menu.
Where is the user manual? Click the book icon in the header; it opens the manual ﬁltered to your role. The ?  icon shows
help for the current page.
What does What’s New show? Release highlights for your persona. A banner appears on your landing page for about 7
days; dismissing it keeps it under the bell icon. Use Mark All as Read to clear the unread dot.
How do I give feedback? Use Share Feedback in the header, or answer the star rating after creating a request or
uploading capacity.
